answer.label: Written by
answer.sourceLine: This is a genuine line from Marcus Aurelius’ Meditations, Book X, section 16, in the classic 1862 translation by George Long. The wording is confirmed verbatim against the George Long text — though the far more viral “Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.” is a modern paraphrase, not any historical translation.

source.heading: The source
source.excerpt: No longer talk at all about the kind of man that a good man ought to be, but be such.
trail: The exact wording appears in George Long’s translation of Meditations X.16 — “No longer talk at all about the kind of man that a good man ought to be, but be such” — confirmed in the Standard Ebooks George Long text ↗.
George Long’s translation was first published in London in 1862 as The Thoughts of the Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus ↗, putting this translation firmly in the public domain.
The punchier “Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one. ↗” is the version that dominates social media — a modern compression of the same passage, matching no classic translation.
source.excerptNote: Book X, §16, in George Long’s translation. Marcus wrote the Meditations in Koine Greek as a private notebook, never intending publication; section 16 is a single terse maxim on acting virtue rather than debating it.

source.rightsNote: The English wording shown is George Long’s translation, first published in London in 1862 — well before 1931 — so it is in the public domain in the United States, as is the ancient Greek original. Note that modern translations of the same passage (e.g. Gregory Hays, 2002) are separately in copyright.

author.name: Marcus Aurelius
author.heading: About Marcus Aurelius
author.bio: Marcus Aurelius Antoninus was Roman emperor from 161 to 180 AD and the last of the “Five Good Emperors.” His private notebook, the Meditations, was written in Greek during military campaigns and never meant for publication; it survives as one of the foundational texts of Stoic philosophy. Its recurring theme is that virtue is proven in action, not in talk — exactly the point of Book X, section 16.

misattribution.heading: The wording to watch
misattribution.intro: The attribution to Marcus Aurelius is correct — but the version most people share is not what he wrote.

items.why: The viral “Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one. ↗” captures the sense of X.16 but matches no historical translation; it is a modern compression, not Marcus’ or any 19th-century translator’s words.

misattribution.truthLine: The literal line is Marcus Aurelius via George Long’s 1862 translation of Meditations X.16: “No longer talk at all about the kind of man that a good man ought to be, but be such ↗.”

context.heading: Why it resonates
lead: Book X of the Meditations is Marcus at his most self-admonishing, and section 16 is one of its shortest entries — a single imperative to stop theorizing about goodness and simply embody it. It reads as a note to himself, which is exactly what it was.

That directness is why the line travels so well, and why it gets smoothed into ever-punchier forms. The genuine George Long wording is elegant; the modern “Be one” version is a slogan. Both point at the same Stoic conviction that character is demonstrated, not discussed.
context.pull: Stop describing the good man. Be him.
